de/bavaria.title: Flag of Bavaria

colors.note: The lozenges (diamonds) of the Bavarian coat of arms.
Bavarian state colour since the Wittelsbach dynasty.

desc:
- The Bavarian flag features the iconic white-and-blue lozenges (Rautenflagge), one of the most recognisable sub-national flags in Europe
- **Construction:** a field of white and blue lozenges (diamonds) arranged in a diagonal pattern
- At least 21 complete lozenges are visible, with a white lozenge in the upper-hoist corner
trivia:
- Bavaria's flag uses blue and white, the colours of the Wittelsbach dynasty
- These colours have represented Bavaria since the 12th century
- Bavaria maintains a distinct identity within modern Germany

de/prussia.title: Flag of the Kingdom of Prussia

colors.note: Prussian state colour; the eagle of Brandenburg.
The Prussian field; Teutonic Order heritage.

desc: - The Prussian flag was black and white, featuring the black Prussian eagle. Prussia was the dominant state that unified Germany in 1871
- **Construction:** a white field bearing a black Prussian eagle centred. The eagle holds an orb and sceptre
trivia:
- Prussia's flag represented one of the most powerful German states historically
- The black eagle symbolised Prussian power and militarism
- Prussia dominated German unification in 1871
